meaning: A machine that scans a paper page and sends a copy over a phone line. Another machine prints the copy.
clues: It sends a message over wires to someone far away.
It can send a whole page, with drawings and pictures, not just words.
A Scottish clockmaker came up with the idea in the 1840s, long before the telephone.
You dialed a number, fed the page into the machine, and pressed start. Each page took about a minute.
It has two words. The first has three letters and starts with F.
assumes: A telegraph sends only Morse code
A teleprinter sends only typed letters

decoys.meaning: A machine that sends messages over a wire as short and long taps of a key, called Morse code.
A machine with a typewriter keyboard. It sends typed words over a wire and prints them far away.
An old copier. Ink is pushed through a typed stencil, so one page can be copied again and again.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: A fax sent a copy of the page as it looked, drawings and all. That still matters when a form has to look just right.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: a scan sent by email. Your phone can scan a paper page and attach it to a message.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: We needed about a minute for each page. Patience was part of the job.
